title: The world's creation is false
hookLine: jag rachnaa sabh jhooth hai: know, friend, that this created world is passing (Salok M9, ang 1429)
last: NAAM — THE NAME IS THE BOAT.

lines: THE SUNRISE, THE BREAD, THE HANDS.
THE SECOND HALF OF THE COUPLET.
cards: When a friend tells you a promise is false, you know what they mean: it was a lie. Someone set out to fool you.
So if you open an English translation of today's salok and read that the world's creation is false, it sounds startling. Is the scripture saying the sunrise is a lie? Your grandmother's hands?
The bread on the table? That's not how Sikhs hear it.
The key is in the second half of the couplet, and in a picture anyone who has played with dry sand knows: pile it into a wall, and it starts slipping the moment you take your hands away.

teach.b: The salok says jag rachnaa sabh jhooth hai, jaan lehu re meet. In paraphrase: all the world's creation is jhooth; understand this, O friend. Then: says Nanak, it does not stay steady, like a wall of sand.
Jhooth is usually translated false. But the salok explains itself. It doesn't say the world is a trick.

teach.h: THIR NAA RAHAI: IT DOESN'T STAY.
teach.b: It says thir naa rahai: it doesn't stay put.

teach.h: BAALOO KEE BHEET: A WALL OF SAND.
teach.b: And it gives the picture: baaloo kee bheet, a wall of sand. A sand wall isn't a lie. It's really there; you can lean on it for a moment.
It just won't hold. That's the sense of jhooth here: not fake, but not lasting. Remember rachnaa, from day five hundred eighty-one: rachnaa raam banaaee, the creation the Lord made.
Same word. The creation is His. What's jhooth is the idea that it will stand forever.

teach.h: RE MEET: SAID TO A FRIEND.
teach.b: And listen to the tone: re meet, O friend. The Guru isn't lecturing a sinner. He's talking to a friend, the way you'd gently tell someone you love not to lean a ladder against loose sand.
So hold it lightly isn't a call to despise anything. Enjoy the house. Love the people.
Do the work well. Just don't lean your whole life against a wall that's already slipping at the top. Lean on what stays, the Name we heard about yesterday.
Six hundred days in, that's worth hearing: everything here is lent, and the lender is the One who stays.

how: This salok is among the ninth Guru's saloks read at the close of every complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib; Sikh teachers explain its jhooth as 'not lasting' rather than 'fake', pointing to its image of a wall of sand.

o: a world that isn't really there at all
not lasting, like a sand wall that won't hold
a deliberate lie told to fool someone

games.q: the world's creation is false — tap the pairs.

s: the salok says the world is a lie or a trick
it explains jhooth itself: the world doesn't stay steady, like a wall of sand.
the salok is addressed to a friend
jaan lehu re meet: understand this, O friend.
the same word rachnaa, creation, appears in a Gauri hymn of the ninth Guru
saadho rachnaa raam banaaee: the creation the Lord made.

games.q: the salok calls the world jhooth. what picture does it give to explain?
o: a wall of sand that doesn't stay steady.
a painting of a fake landscape.
games.why: says Nanak, it does not stay steady, like a wall of sand. jhooth here means not lasting, not fake.

practice: Think of one thing you've been leaning on with your whole weight, a plan, a status, someone's approval, and picture it as a wall of sand you're pressed against.
Gently take one step back: you don't knock it down, you just stand on your own feet, near it, not against it. If you pray, lean on Waheguru instead for these breaths.

wordCard.voice: Jhooth. The salok calls the world's creation jhooth, not because it's fake, but because, like a wall of sand, it doesn't stay steady, and it says so as one friend to another.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: jhooth, usually 'false'; in this salok, what doesn't last, like a wall of sand.

carryVoice: Your line: hold it lightly. The wall is real; it just won't hold. Six hundred days, and counting.

sources.ref: Salok Mahalla 9, salok 49, 'jag rachnaa sabh jhooth hai' (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1429)
Raag Gauri, Mahalla 9, 'saadho rachnaa raam banaaee' (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 219)
